what_a_verdict_means.AMEND: The disposition stands, but a named defect in the drafted text is owed a correction in a successor map, judged by a seat that did not draft it.
what_a_verdict_means.REJECT: The disposition is wrong. The entry returns to a drafting seat, and a seat that did not draft the redraft judges it.
what_a_verdict_means.finding: No verdict: a matter outside any one draft, each with its recommendation and whose it is.

rows.title: new prose (kickoff items 2 and 3)
rows.finding: Completing a move is not new prose under L2's standard ("with no new prose") when all three conditions hold. (ii) The remainder fails a ratified gate (the validator's 40-word move floor) or no longer reaches the card's own terminus. (iii) The added words are the entry's own R1 row's stronger line, verbatim except for a declared change of voice. Josiah adopted each R1 row as presented, stronger line included, so that text is ruled record, not new argument. Anything beyond it is new prose and needs its own ratification. #1, #7 and #62 meet all three. #14 is owed a completion under (ii). #40's re-authored move meets (iii), and its trigger is the under-strength shape R1-006 ruled.
rows.recommendation: Adopt this as the reading of L2's 'no new prose' for moves. It keeps the standard's intent: cards ship on text the ruled record already holds.
